scope: Constants of the turn_taking_projection task: how a mono mix is split into one channel per speaker, and how VAP frames are read against caller-given turns, IPUs and backchannels. None is fitted to labelled turn-taking data; each derivation says what it was chosen from. Measurements behind the separation default are in specs/20261017-110000-dyadic-turn-taking/.

mask_ramp_seconds.derivation: Owner's specification (50 ms raised-cosine ramps outside each diarization segment). Half of one VAP frame at 10 Hz, so a ramp never spans a full frame and a segment edge moves the projection by at most one frame.

assignment_hop_seconds.derivation: Energy-envelope hop for matching separated sources to diarization speakers. 20 ms is the conventional short-time analysis hop for speech energy; five per VAP frame, so the envelope resolves every frame-level segment boundary.

separation_chunk_seconds.derivation: Length of the windows a separator sees. Each window is assigned to the caller's speakers on its own, so a separator's arbitrary source order cannot swap channels for the rest of a recording; 60 s holds several turns of each speaker in a conversation, which the assignment needs to tell the two sources apart.

separation_overlap_seconds.derivation: Cross-fade between consecutive separation windows: long enough to cover one IPU boundary, short against the 60 s window (3 % recomputed).

projection_window_seconds.derivation: Window before a speaker change over which the next speaker's p_now is read as the shift prediction. Inside p_now's own 0-600 ms horizon, so a frame in the window projects onto the moment of the change.

pause_read_offset_seconds.derivation: Hold/shift is read starting this long after a pause opens, so the frame that still contains the last syllable's tail is skipped. Half a VAP frame.

pause_read_seconds.derivation: How long into a pause p_now is averaged for the hold/shift call: two VAP frames, the earliest a response could be made after the pause opens.

min_pause_seconds.derivation: Shortest mutual silence counted as a hold/shift opportunity: offset plus read window plus no less than one frame of margin; shorter gaps are within-word stops, not floor-transfer points.

shift_probability_threshold.derivation: p_now is normalised across the two speakers, so 0.5 is the point at which the model says the other speaker is more likely to hold the floor next; not a tuned operating point. The continuous score is reported beside every call, so a caller can choose another.

bc_peak_threshold.derivation: A backchannel opportunity is a local maximum of p_bc above this. 0.5 is where the backchannel head's sigmoid favours a backchannel; not tuned. Peak heights are reported, so a caller can apply another.

bc_peak_min_separation_seconds.derivation: Minimum spacing between two opportunities of one listener: shorter than an IPU, so consecutive IPUs each get their own, and longer than one backchannel token, so one rising edge is not counted twice.

bc_response_window_seconds.derivation: A backchannel answers an opportunity when its onset falls this long before to after the peak. The early side admits a listener who anticipates the model (the model is causal and peaks on evidence the listener may already have); the late side allows a one-second reaction, the order of a listener's response latency after a pause opens.

backchannel_max_seconds.derivation: When the caller gives no backchannel list, a listener IPU at most this long that lies inside the other speaker's turn is taken as a backchannel. Single-token backchannels (yeah, mm-hm, right) run 0.2-0.7 s.
